note: Items are atomic properties, not matches to a historical fix. A different analysis that establishes the property is a hit. Document ids here are the original ids; scorer tasks translate them to the neutral ids the output uses. Expect and positive items: hit, miss, not_assessed (the output never addresses the target text), uncertain. Must-not items: violated, not_violated, uncertain. Typed outputs earn an item only through a comparator flag or record on the matching text and property (scorer rules); typing a field without a matching flag or record is not a hit. Typed matches: E1 owner_unresolved; E7a verifier_unassigned; E7b independence_unstated; E4b adopted_without_owner, owner_decision_not_shown or authority_not_established naming the owner F-041 names. deficient_provenance alone never decides an entailment item or a must-not.

items.text: The planner describes the Host performing the container's removal as how the work is done.
The planner states, as an obligation, that removal must be credited to or attributed to the Host specifically (not merely observed, or the container merely absent).
The planner states the requirement for an independent post-exit check that the original container is absent.
The planner states that a failed, never-started or unknown Host removal must be reported distinctly, not as a clean cancel.

Identifies, in F-043's own wording, that who must bring about the container removal is not plainly assigned: removal is to be 'observed' without saying who removes it, next to 'Host owns ... exact stop'. A reading that this is resolved elsewhere in the packet still counts if the gap in F-043's wording is identified.

must_not.text: Proposes dropping or weakening the independent post-exit absence check.
Proposes dropping the requirement to distinguish confirmed removal, removal failure and unknown cleanup.

items.text: Treats the requirement that a failed or never-started Host removal be reported as failure (not clean cancel) as supported by the parent plan's requirement to distinguish removal outcomes.
Identifies the requirement for an affirmative result that distinguishes the Host's own removal from 'already missing' as going beyond what the parents state.
Identifies the amended rule's 'positively attained normal-removal witness' as stronger than what the parents state.

Identifies that the change to the clean-cancel requirement is not shown to be decided by the party the documents name as owning that meaning (F-041 assigns lifecycle admission and receipt semantics to RL): either it is adopted by a different party, or no decision by that owner appears in the documents, or it should be routed to that owner. This does not require knowing whether the owner approved it outside the documents.
Identifies that Host-positive removal is made a requirement regardless of how removal is realized, and that the specific parent text it cites does not state that.
Identifies that ruling out engine automatic removal lacks support in the parent text.
Identifies that the statement that the H1-H5 requirements are unchanged includes Host affirmative and attributable removal, which the named parents do not state.

must_not.text: Flags the requirement to report a failed Host removal as failure as unsupported.
Treats the amended rule as optional or ignorable, rather than as something to route to its owner.
Flags F-DEC's requirements that destructive effects must not reach another object, or that an observer independently confirms disposition after exit, as unsupported.
Proposes dropping or weakening the independent post-exit absence check.

items.text: Identifies that the system must verify that the covered execution has stopped, but the text does not name who verifies.
Identifies that the text does not state that the verifier must be independent of the party that terminates the execution.

must_not.text: States that B-1539 already requires an independent verifier.

items.text: Recognizes that item 2 assigns termination to a designated termination actor and requires an observer independent of the killer's claim.

must_not.text: Raises a bundled-responsibility or unassigned-responsibility flag on the termination and observer obligation in item 2. Flags on other parts of the document are not violations.

items.text: Recognizes that the renderer itself initiates, performs and reports the deletion, and that no independent check is required.

must_not.text: Flags the renderer's cleanup obligation as bundled or unassigned, or demands an independent verifier the contract expressly does not require.

items.text: Classifies the review's requirement that the Host itself perform and attribute the removal, plus the independent absence check, as stated by the contract's recorded owner decision.

must_not.text: Flags the review's Host-attributed removal requirement as unsupported or beyond the parent.

items.text: Classifies the automatic-removal option and the runner issuing the stop as the authors' revisable choices within the requirement.
Classifies the acceptance statement as matching the parent requirement.

must_not.text: Flags the automatic-removal choice or the runner issuing the stop as a new or strengthened requirement.
Flags the acceptance statement as unsupported or changed.
